title: AgentFlow Event Envelope (v1)
description: The minimal JSON envelope carried by every Kafka record produced by AgentFlow (glossary §6, task S06-01). It is identical for every event; only {@code eventType} and {@code payload} differ. {@code tenantId} is a routing/correlation field only and is NEVER an authorization source — the consumer re-checks ownership against PostgreSQL (invariant 1). The envelope is versioned independently of the per-event payload vocabulary: breaking envelope changes create a new {@code schemaVersion} (new major schema, see contracts/AGENTS.md), while new event types are additive and never change this file. Secret, full-prompt and full-document data never enter the payload or the headers (invariants 7 and 8); the concrete payload is a typed object with an explicit field allowlist, defined per event in contracts/events/json-schema/ (S06-02).

eventId.description: Unique, immutable id of this event, assigned by the producer. Used for idempotent outbox publishing (by event_id, S06-07/S06-08) and inbox deduplication (S06-04, S06-10). Exactly-once is never promised (at-least-once, ADR-003).

eventType.description: The event name. The concrete vocabulary and the topic/version naming (topic-name ending in .v<N>, e.g. agentflow.workflow.run-requested.v1 per glossary §6) are fixed by the topic catalogue (S06-02) and the event catalog (S06-16). New event types are additive; this field never changes an existing event's meaning.

schemaVersion.description: The version of THIS envelope schema (the file, not the event). Bump on any breaking change to the envelope shape — a removed or renamed field, or a change to the required set — following the compatibility rule in contracts/AGENTS.md (new major schema). Adding an optional field is compatible and does not bump this value.

occurredAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which the event occurred, assigned by the producer and written with the timestamptz column in the outbox (invariant 10). Injectable Clock in tests (S06-14).

tenantId.description: The owning tenant. CORRELATION AND ROUTING ONLY — never an authorization source. The producer scopes the event to the tenant of the verified security context / stored run, and the consumer re-checks ownership against PostgreSQL before acting (invariant 1); a tenantId arriving in Kafka headers is not trusted for authorization. Read and filter by the (tenantId, aggregateId) pair.

aggregateType.description: The aggregate the event is about (run, step, document, ...). The concrete set and the topic/key strategy per aggregate are fixed by the topic catalogue (S06-02): workflow events key by tenantId:runId, document events by tenantId:documentId.

aggregateId.description: The aggregate instance id the event is scoped to: the runId for a run event, the stepRunId for a step event, or the documentId for a document event.

correlationId.description: Identifies the whole operation/correlation chain, shared by every event of one run from request to completion. Propagated in the Kafka headers alongside the trace parent (S06-12). Not an authorization input.

causationId.description: The id of the event that caused this one, enabling replay and diagnostics. Null for the first event in a correlation chain (there is no predecessor); set to the triggering event's eventId otherwise. Propagated in the Kafka headers (S06-12).

payload.description: Event-specific DATA. Must contain only redacted, non-secret fields: never a secret, API key, full prompt, full model output, full document, or any untrusted content treated as data (invariants 7 and 8). The concrete shape is a typed object with an explicit field allowlist (additionalProperties: false), defined per event in contracts/events/json-schema/ (S06-02) so a disallowed field is rejected at the payload schema. An empty object is valid for an event with no data. At-least-once delivery means a producer may retry; payload side effects are idempotent (S06-05, S06-10).
